name: Swiss Confederation Founded
summary: The Forest Cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden sign the Federal Charter at Rütli Meadow, pledging mutual defense. The confederation gradually adds more cantons; victories at Morgarten (1315) and Sempach (1386) establish Swiss infantry as the most feared in Europe. The name "Switzerland" derives from Schwyz.

_quarry.structural_significance: Creates the oldest surviving federal constitution; the Swiss model of armed neutrality and confederal governance influences modern state theory; Swiss mercenaries reshape European warfare by making infantry the dominant military force.
